items.new: With a long, weary hoist the jaw is dragged on board, as if it were an anchor; and when the proper time comes — some few days after the other work — Queequeg, Daggoo, and Tashtego, being all accomplished dentists, are set to drawing teeth. With a keen cutting-spade, Queequeg lances the gums; then the jaw is lashed down to ringbolts, and a tackle being rigged from aloft, they drag out these teeth, as Michigan oxen drag stumps of old oaks out of wild woodlands. There are generally forty-two teeth in all; in old whales, much worn down, but undecayed, and not filled in our artificial fashion. The jaw is afterwards sawn into slabs, and piled away like joists for building houses.

items.new: In thought, a fine human brow is like the East when troubled with the morning. In the repose of the pasture, the curled brow of the bull has a touch of the grand in it. When the elephant pushes heavy cannon up mountain passes, his brow is majestic. Human or animal, the mystical brow is like that great golden seal affixed by the German emperors to their decrees. It signifies — "God: done this day by my hand." But in most creatures, and even in man himself, the brow is very often a mere strip of alpine land lying along the snow line. Few are the foreheads which, like Shakespeare's or Melancthon's, rise so high and come down so low that the eyes themselves seem clear, eternal, tideless mountain lakes; and in the forehead's wrinkles above them you seem to track the antlered thoughts coming down there to drink, as Highland hunters track the deer's prints in the snow. But in the great Sperm Whale, this high and mighty godlike dignity inherent in the brow is so immensely amplified that, gazing on it in that full front view, you feel the Deity and the dread powers more forcibly than in looking at any other object in living nature. For you see no one point precisely; not one distinct feature is revealed; no nose, eyes, ears or mouth; no face — he has none, properly speaking; nothing but that one broad firmament of a forehead, pleated with riddles, dumbly lowering with the doom of boats, and ships, and men. Nor does this wondrous brow diminish in profile, though viewed that way its grandeur does not overpower you so much. In profile you plainly see that horizontal, half-moon-shaped hollow in the middle of the forehead which, in man, is Lavater's mark of genius.

items.new: In the full-grown creature the skull will measure at least twenty feet in length. Unhinge the lower jaw, and the side view of this skull is like the side of a moderately inclined plane resting throughout on a level base. But in life — as we have seen elsewhere — this inclined plane is filled up at an angle, and almost squared off, by the enormous mass of the junk and sperm lying on top of it. At the high end the skull forms a crater to bed that part of the mass; while under the long floor of this crater — in another cavity seldom more than ten inches long and as many deep — lies the mere handful of this monster's brain. In life the brain is at least twenty feet from his apparent forehead; it is hidden away behind its vast outworks, like the innermost citadel within the enlarged fortifications of Quebec. It is secreted in him like a choice casket, so much so that I have known some whalemen who flatly deny that the Sperm Whale has any other brain than that palpable semblance of one formed by the cubic yards of his sperm magazine. Given its strange folds, courses and convolutions, they think it more in keeping with the idea of his general might to regard that mystic part of him as the seat of his intelligence.
